headline: INTC priced a $20bn share sale at $95, upsized from $15bn, hours after the stock closed down 4.06%.
quick: Intel sold $20bn of new stock, upsized from the $15bn it announced that morning. It priced 210,526,315 shares at $95.00 after Monday's close, raising about $19.7bn net. That is roughly a full year of the company's own building costs, raised in a single day.

The day split technology in two, and it was not a risk-off day. The five that fell are all AI hardware: MRVL, INTC, NVDA, NBIS and AAPL. The seven that rose are software and platforms. QQQ moved just -0.30%.

Marvell fell 4.65%, the largest fall of the twelve, and announced nothing. It opened 4.2% higher at $227.96 and gave the whole gap back inside thirty minutes. The close sits 9.35% under the session high.

macro.dt: Oil rose toward $80 a barrel after a weekend passed without progress on the Middle East. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.705% Monday from 4.639% on Friday, and was quoted near 4.733% early Tuesday
macro.dd: Oil is an input cost that shows up in inflation about a month later. That matters here through one number: the yield used to discount profits arriving years from now. Friday's rally on weak payrolls assumed that yield keeps falling. Two sessions later it is going the other way, which takes back part of the reason these stocks rose.

macro.dt: QQQ closed 720.87, -0.30%, and sits 3.71% below its 52-week high of 748.65. Seven of these twelve rose and five fell
macro.dd: It disagrees, and the disagreement is the story. A rising oil price and a rising yield should hurt the longest-duration names hardest, yet Palantir led the twelve higher. What actually fell was the hardware: chips and the companies that rent them out. That is a rotation inside technology, not a verdict on rates.

macro.dt: Every one of the twelve traded below its own average volume. Intel ran 10.6% light on the day it announced a $20bn equity raise, and that was among the heaviest participation of the twelve
macro.dd: Thin volume on a day with a headline event means few holders changed their minds. Prices moved because sellers met a smaller crowd of buyers, not because a large number of investors repriced anything. Read every move below as provisional in that sense: Wednesday's inflation print is the first thing that will draw real volume.

entries.move: -4.06% · Monday close, settled, before the pricing
entries.happened: Intel announced a $15bn share offering before Monday's open, then upsized it to $20bn and priced it after the close.
figures: Priced 210,526,315 shares at $95.00, for gross proceeds of $20bn and net proceeds of about $19.7bn. The offering is expected to close 12 August
Upsized from the $15bn announced pre-open the same day. Underwriters hold a 30-day option on 31,578,947 further shares, worth about $3.0bn more
Intel reported 5.044bn shares outstanding as of 17 July. The base deal is therefore about 4.2% dilution, or 4.8% if the option is exercised in full
The $95 price is 6.5% below Friday's $101.65 close and 2.6% below Monday's $97.52. Stated use of proceeds: general corporate purposes, including capital expenditure and working capital
Intel has guided 2026 capital spending above $20bn, raised from $18bn, with high-volume manufacturing on its 14A process targeted for 2028

Monday close $97.52, -4.06%, on volume 10.6% below its own average. Filings not read: sec.gov is unreachable from this environment, so the terms above come from the company's release as carried in coverage
entries.why: Equity is the costliest money a company can raise, because it hands new owners a permanent share of every future profit. Choosing it over debt says the board wanted the cash certain rather than cheap, and wanted it now. What the sum buys is the point: it covers roughly a full year of Intel's building programme in one stroke. That converts an open question about whether Intel can afford to chase TSMC into a narrower one about whether it can execute, and the answer does not arrive until 14A reaches volume.

foot.v: Half of it. The window is Monday's close, settled, and it sits between the two announcements. It reflects a $15bn deal of unknown price. The extra $5bn and the $95 level landed after the bell, so Monday's -4.06% is not a reaction to the terms that were actually struck.
A named external foundry customer is disclosed with a dollar value attached. The raise funds capacity; it does not fill it.
12 August, the offering closes. Q3 results late October, no confirmed date.

entries.strength_label: Major move · no company news · sector
entries.happened: Marvell fell 4.65% with nothing announced, after opening more than four per cent higher.
figures: Closed $208.56, -4.65%, from $218.72. That is the largest fall of the twelve
It opened $227.96, some 4.2% above Friday, and touched $230.07. The first thirty-minute bar ran all the way down to $215.15, so the entire gap was gone before 10:00 ET
The close is 9.35% below the session high, the widest high-to-close reversal of the twelve. The last half hour alone fell from $214.11 to $208.56 on 2.6M shares, the heaviest half hour since the open
Volume 20.4M against a 24.0M average, 15.0% light. It sits 36.78% below its 52-week high
Not news: the AI memory platform launch was 4 August at FMS 2026, and the $250M three-year India expansion also predates this window. Neither was announced on Monday
entries.why: Nothing about the order book changed on Monday, so what moved was the price investors will pay for it. Marvell sells custom silicon designed into a small number of hyperscaler programmes, which means its revenue is a bet on next year's data-centre budgets rather than this quarter's shipments. A stock built that way swings on belief, and it carries roughly twice the market's sensitivity in both directions. The round trip from plus four to minus five, on no information at all, is that sensitivity showing.

foot.v: There is no news to price. The window is Monday's close, settled. The opening gap was the market still paying for last week's product news, and the session took it back.
The 27 August guidance puts a dated dollar figure on custom-silicon bookings rather than a growth rate.
27 August, Q2 FY27, after the close.

entries.strength_label: Notable move · no company news · sector
entries.happened: Nvidia fell 2.86% with no dated company event in the window.
figures: Closed $217.55, -2.86%, from $223.96, on volume 108.1M against a 130.0M average, 16.8% light
It sits 8.03% below its 52-week high of $236.54. The session opened $223.45 and closed near its low of $216.77
entries.why: Nvidia is the price-setter for this whole group, so when it falls on no news the read is about the trade rather than the company. Intel's raise is the thing to watch, and it cuts both ways. Twenty billion dollars of new capacity aimed at AI silicon is a future competitor being funded in public. It is also years away, because nothing ships from a process that reaches volume in 2028.

foot.v: A hyperscaler trims its 2027 capital budget at an August update.

entries.strength_label: Notable move · no company news · one day out
entries.happened: Nebius fell 2.05% with nothing announced, one session before its Q2 results.
figures: Closed $184.11, -2.05%, after reaching $196.13 intraday. The close is 6.13% below that high
Volume 14.7M against a 26.7M average, 44.9% light, the lightest participation of the twelve
It sits 38.60% below its 52-week high, the widest gap of the twelve. Robinhood is inside a rounding error of it at 38.57%

Q2 lands Wednesday 12 August before the open, company-confirmed on 29 July. Analyst expectations cited in coverage run to roughly $572M to $585M of revenue, against $399M in Q1, with losses still expected
entries.why: Nebius rents out computing capacity, and it has funded far more of it than it currently bills for. The gap between money already spent and revenue that mostly starts in 2027 is the entire argument over the stock. Wednesday is when that gap either gets a contracted number attached to it or does not. Falling into the print on the lightest volume here says few holders wanted to take a position before finding out.

foot.v: Nothing to price yet. The window is Monday's close, settled, and it reflects positioning rather than information.
Wednesday sets a dated backlog figure against the capacity already paid for.
12 August, Q2 results before the open, company-confirmed.

entries.happened: Palantir rose 1.87% with nothing announced, the largest gain of the twelve again.
figures: Closed $175.23, +1.87%, from $172.01, after touching $179.60. Volume 55.3M against a 61.8M average, 10.6% light
It sits 15.56% below its 52-week high of $207.52. Q2 was reported 3 August and is outside this window
entries.why: Palantir rose while yields rose, which is the opposite of Friday's logic. That leaves the software-over-hardware rotation as the explanation, and it fits: money left the companies that build AI capacity and went to the ones that sell what runs on it. The move is worth less than Friday's because the volume behind it was lighter.

foot.v: 12 August CPI. Q3 results early November.

entries.strength_label: Notable move · Sunday report now settled
entries.happened: Apple fell 1.62%, settling the reaction to Sunday's report that it is testing Chinese memory chips.
figures: Closed $308.26, -1.62%, from $313.33. It opened $306.83, so the fall happened at the open and the stock then recovered to close at its session high
Volume 43.4M against a 63.2M average, 31.3% light. It sits 10.54% below its 52-week high
Monday was the ex-dividend date for the $0.27 dividend declared 30 July, worth about 0.09% of the price. It explains almost none of the fall

Excluded: a broker cut Apple to its lowest rating on 10 August and lowered its target to $263.66. Ratings and targets are commentary and this brief leaves them out, but it is a competing explanation for the same move
entries.why: Yesterday's edition called this provisional on premarket alone and said the open would settle it. It has. The memory-cost problem is now a settled price rather than an overnight indication, which matters because Apple's gross margin is the number its whole valuation rests on. A cost it cannot control has to land on that margin, on the retail price, or on units sold.

foot.v: Now yes, and this is the settled version of yesterday's provisional read. The window is Monday's close. The gap happened at the open and the stock spent the day recovering, which is a market that took the point and then thought better of the size of it.
Apple confirms memory supply locked at fixed prices through the iPhone cycle.

readthrough.title: The market funded the AI build-out and sold the builders, on the same afternoon
readthrough.body: Monday did two contradictory things at once. Intel placed $20bn of new stock to pay for AI manufacturing capacity, and had to raise the size of the deal because demand exceeded what it first offered. In the same session Marvell fell 4.65% and Nvidia 2.86%, on no company news at all. Institutions bought a chipmaker's paper at $95 and sold the chipmakers. Both trades can be right, because they are bets on different clocks. The equity buyers are underwriting capacity that reaches volume production in 2028. The sellers are marking down what they will pay today for revenue expected in 2027. Rising oil and a 10-year yield back up at 4.705% hurt the second group and barely touch the first. Now the asymmetry worth keeping. Intel fell 4.06% on a real, quantified event: about 4.2% dilution at a known discount. Marvell fell further, 4.65%, on nothing whatsoever. The stock with concrete bad news fell less than the stock with no news, which is the difference between pricing an event and repricing a belief. The second is the less stable of the two, and Wednesday's inflation print is aimed straight at it.

note.title: What is not news, what could not be checked, and one gap in the data
note.body: One of the twelve carried a dated event in this window: Intel. Apple's was Sunday's memory report, already covered in yesterday's edition and settled by Monday's session rather than announced anew. The other ten announced nothing qualifying, so their moves are the rotation, the sector, or a continuation. Excluded on date: Marvell's AI memory launch was 4 August and its $250M India expansion earlier still; Palantir's Q2 was 3 August; Alphabet's DeepMind departures were 5 August; Meta's New Mexico ruling was 7 August; Tesla's Terafab commitment was 6 August and its $10.1bn solar filing dates to 22 July or 6 August depending on the report, all of them before this window despite fresh coverage on 10 August. Excluded as commentary: the broker downgrade of Apple and target changes elsewhere. sec.gov is blocked by this environment's proxy, so Intel's offering terms are taken from the company's release as carried in coverage and not read against the filing itself; intel.com and the main wires are also blocked here. No premarket data this run: the price feed's plan does not include extended hours, so every window quoted above is Monday's settled close and no premarket indication is given for any ticker. All prices and volumes come from the Twelve Data API. Press coverage of Marvell on Monday described it as rising, because much of it was written before the reversal.
